title: Adelaide University Engineers Synthetic Area Spread to Unlock High-Sensitivity Absolute Quantum Magnetometers - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Adelaide University's QuaNTeG showed in Physical Review Applied that adding 'bare' superconducting loops to uniform 2D SQIF arrays creates a synthetic area spread, giving a zero-field anti-peak for absolute magnetometry without varying loop sizes that degrade sensitivity. Devices were fabricated on SEEQC's commercial foundry process and the concept is under PCT patent application.

insights.claim: DC SQUIDs are among the most sensitive magnetic field detectors but their periodic voltage-flux response prevents them from directly serving as absolute magnetometers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains why absolute superconducting magnetometry has remained a niche requiring workarounds.
insights.locator: While conventional DC SQUIDs rank among

insights.claim: Conventional SQIF arrays create a zero-flux anti-peak using loops with incommensurate areas, but varying loop sizes changes cell inductance, destabilizing the screening parameter betaL and compromising junction sensitivity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Identifies the design compromise the new method removes.
insights.quote: varying loop sizes drastically alters the inductance (L) of individual cells, destabilizing the critical screening parameter βL
insights.locator: While conventional DC SQUIDs rank among

insights.claim: The Adelaide team showed physical area variation is mathematically unnecessary: bare loops without Josephson junctions inject an inductive flux term that Kirchhoff constraints map onto active junctions as an effective synthetic area spread.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A geometry-uniform design could simplify fabrication and improve yield of quantum sensors.
insights.quote: demonstrated that physical area variations are mathematically unnecessary

insights.claim: A 46x16 mixed array with 16 junction rows separated by pairs of bare-loop rows produced a sharp reproducible central anti-peak at zero flux, absent in a 16x16 uniform baseline array.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Experimental, not just theoretical, validation of the approach.

insights.claim: Test arrays were fabricated through SEEQC's commercial Nb/AlOx/Nb tri-layer process on 150 mm silicon wafers at 4.5 kA/cm2 critical current density, validating manufacturability on standard superconducting fab lines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Commercial-foundry fabrication shortens the path from lab to product and benefits foundry operators like SEEQC.

insights.claim: The concept is protected under international patent application PCT/AU2025/050991.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Patent filing signals intent to license or spin out the technology.

insights.claim: Target applications include magnetoencephalography brain imaging, low-noise RF receivers, and quantum hardware readout.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Medical imaging and RF sensing offer nearer-term quantum-sensing revenue than quantum computing.
